evidence.description: The init method uses 'Task { await self.retrieveStoredCredentials() }' to perform async work without providing a mechanism to await completion or handle the lifecycle of the task.

candidates.explanation: The initializer of the class triggers an unstructured Task to perform an asynchronous operation (retrieveStoredCredentials). This can lead to race conditions during initialization because the object is considered initialized and available for use before the credential retrieval completes.
candidates.title: Unstructured Task in Initializer

candidates.explanation: The class uses a shared singleton instance for the authentication service. While common, this can make unit testing difficult by introducing global state and making it harder to isolate side effects or mock dependencies.
candidates.title: Singleton Pattern

evidence.description: if let authProvider = auth0Provider as? NativeToWebSSOAuth0Provider

candidates.explanation: The class performs a forced downcast to a concrete type (NativeToWebSSOAuth0Provider) to access specific functionality. This violates the Dependency Inversion Principle and makes the service tightly coupled to a specific implementation of the auth provider.
candidates.title: Tight Coupling via Downcasting

evidence.description: Task { await dispatchAuthStateChange(isLoggedIn: isLoggedIn, fromCredentialRetrieval: false) }

candidates.explanation: The setupTokensWithCredentials method launches an unstructured Task to dispatch state changes. Since this is a private helper method, it provides no way for the caller to know when the state change has actually occurred, which can lead to UI inconsistencies or race conditions.
candidates.title: Unstructured Task in Helper Method

candidates.explanation: The class contains a public property 'skipUserInfoFetch' used to toggle behavior during testing. Hardcoding test-specific flags inside production logic is an anti-pattern; it is better to use dependency injection or separate mock objects for testing.
candidates.title: Test Flag in Production Code
